assertions.name: qpoch_valuation_is_n
assertions.source: ν((q;q)_n) = n for every n in range — validates the valuation routine

assertions.name: masbaum_valuation_meets_proved_floor
assertions.source: ν(T^Mas_n) ≥ 2n — the Lean theorem checked against the real Masbaum coefficients

assertions.name: valuation_additivity
assertions.source: ν(T^Mas_n) = ν(C_n) + 2n — the two measurements certify each other

description: Measures the (1−q)-adic valuation at q = 1 of the real 5₂ Masbaum level terms T^Mas_n = C_n·(q;q)_n², to test whether the proved level-map coefficient floor (1−q)^{2n+3m} (QOU/QBeta/LevelMapValuation.lean, sub_one_pow_dvd_coeff_combined) is tight on the real data. Valuations computed exactly by repeated synthetic division by (q−1) over the integers — no floats, no tolerance. Gates: ν((q;q)_n) = n on the same code path; ν(T^Mas_n) ≥ 2n (the theorem, machine-checked); ν(T^Mas_n) = ν(C_n) + 2n (cross-certification of the two measurements). auditOnly; no c_k wired; no fit; no bridge claimed.

data.verdict: The proved floor ν ≥ 2n is TIGHT on the real data (ν(C_n) = 0 for every measured n ≤ 12): the Masbaum coefficient contributes NO extra vanishing at q = 1, so (1−q)^{2n+3m} is exactly the forced content of a single-level bridge coefficient and the degree bound deg ≥ 2n+3m cannot be improved by this argument. auditOnly.
